headline: Capitals’ Wilson ejected for boarding Panthers’ Vilmanis
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Capitals forward Tom Wilson was ejected for boarding Panthers defenseman Vilmanis, drilling him from behind into the boards and drawing a major penalty and a game misconduct. The report doesn't say whether the league will look at it further.

The immediate cost is on the ice. A major means five minutes on the penalty kill, and our numbers say the Panthers are well placed to use it: they generate 1.14 expected goals per game on the power play (expected goals measures the quality of chances, not just goals), against 0.5 for the Capitals. Washington's penalty kill allows 0.8 expected goals per game, solid enough, but a full five minutes tests it. The Capitals are otherwise a sound team so far this season, with a 50.5 percent share of expected goals overall and 53 percent at five-on-five. Florida sits at 53.6 percent overall, and has scored 2.4 goals fewer than its chances suggest, so a few power-play goals would help the Panthers' results catch up to their play.
